newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors summon Hanbo founder for probe.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors summon Hanbo founder for probe.

text.p: South Korea's state prosecutors said on Thursday they were summoning the founder of the troubled Hanbo Group, Chung Tae-soo, over a loan scandal involving the conglomerate's steelmaking unit.
"We asked Mr Chung Tae-soo to report to the prosecution office by 3:00 p.m. (0600 GMT) today," a prosecutor involved in the probe into Hanbo said.
The prosecutors have already questioned top aides to Chung on how billions of dollars of loans were funnelled to Hanbo Steel Co, flagship of South Korea's 14th largest conglomerate.
Hanbo Steel, the country's second largest steelmaker, filed for court receivership on Tuesday after piling up five trillion won ($5.8 billion) of loans from 61 banks and financial institutions.
Hanbo Steel defaulted on debt repayments last week.
